newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable in quiet trading.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Tuesday on thin buying interest due to the Ramadan fasting month, traders said.
"The market has been quiet since Monday because of the fasting month," said one trader in Jakarta.
He said state logistics agency BULOG's intervention to stabilise olein prices had expanded to Cirebon and Surabaya from Jakarta and that the price was set at 1,440 rupiah/kg.
"The market operation has expanded to other cities. I heard some traders sell olein at 1,435 rupiah/kg -- maybe they just want to test the market," he said.
Traders said olein prices usually fluctuate during the fasting month which made players reluctant to take positions.
Traders in the north Sumatran city of Medan said crude palm oil was done at an equivalent of 1,250 rupiah/kg at a 500-tonne tender, higher than the previous tender price of 1,225.
They said the market did not feel the impact of the report by crop forecaster Ivan Wong that Malaysia's palm oil output in January is estimated to fall 9.0 percent from December's 637,865 tonnes.
Traders said export prices of palm oil were slackening for lack of fresh factors.
Data from Belawan Port showed that MT Prabu will leave Dumai port on Tuesday for Cirebon with 2,000 tonnes of palm olein.
The TB Buhilla will leave Tanjung Sarang Elang port for Labuhan Bulik with 825 tonnes of crude palm oil.
